sources.cite: Google Cloud, Professional Cloud Developer certification exam guide: Section 1 Designing highly scalable, secure, and reliable cloud-native applications (~32%), Section 2 Building and testing (~23%), Section 3 Configuring for deployment (~24%), Section 4 Integrating with Google Cloud services (~21%)

Quoted: 1.1 'Using traffic splitting strategies (e.g., gradual rollouts, rollbacks, A/B testing) on a new service on Cloud Run or GKE'; 1.3 'Creating signed URLs to grant access to Cloud Storage objects'.

sources.cite: Google Cloud documentation, Cloud SQL for PostgreSQL: Managed Connection Pooling overview
sources.note: Read through a summarizing fetch of the Italian page on 2026-11-17. Relevant text: managed connection pooling helps scale workloads while optimizing resource use and connection latency, most useful for many short-lived connections or connection spikes such as serverless apps; it requires a Cloud SQL Enterprise Plus instance; transaction mode (the default, recommended for short-lived connections) and session mode; 'enabling managed connection pooling on an existing instance restarts the database'.

sources.cite: Google Cloud documentation, Cloud SQL for PostgreSQL: Configure database flags (supported flags table)
sources.note: Read through a summarizing fetch on 2026-11-17 (first 100,000 characters). Relevant text: max_connections' default depends on instance memory (25 to 1,000); changing it requires a restart; 'When you set, remove, or modify a flag for a database instance, the database might be restarted.' The PostgreSQL error 'sorry, too many clients already' is from PostgreSQL itself (to verify against the PostgreSQL documentation).
